tei:bibl.tei:title: אִתִּי מִלְּבָנוֹן
Itti MiLvanon, a yotser piyyut for Shabbat haGadol by Rabbi Binyamin bar Zeraḥ
tei:bibl.tei:author: Binyamin bar Zeraḥ
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: The Minhag Ashkenaz (Western Ashkenazi) yotser (piyyut inserted into the beginning of the first blessing of the Shema service) for Shabbat haGadol, by Binyamin bar Zeraḥ. Also recited by some eastern Ashkenazim, although not as commonly as Aamir Mistater (the standard in Minhag Polin). Translated here with preserved acrostic and rhyme scheme. This piyyut uses the language of Song of Songs to retell the story of the exodus via the language of a romantic relationship.

While the translator normally translates God’s pronouns as They/Them, this poem allegorizes the relationship between God and Israel as that of a groom and bride, so he chose to use He/Him in this case.
